name: Atomic and Molecular Clusters

papers.title: Electronically Rather Than Geometrically Driven Concerted Proton Transfer under Graphene Confinement
papers.abstract: Proton transfer in water is a common yet mechanistically non-trivial phenomenon that underpins proton conduction and chemical reactivity. However, how confinement alters it, and whether the changes are driven by geometry or by electronic interaction, remains far from fully understood. Here, using a water hexamer confined between two graphene sheets as a model system, we combine coupled-cluster and first-principles calculations with energy decomposition to investigate how confinement alters its concerted proton transfer. We find that tightening the confinement lowers the electronic proton-transfer barrier. This reduction does not arise from the geometric distortion of the ring, which merely accompanies the confinement, but from the orbital stabilization of the transition state by the graphene walls. These results demonstrate that the proton-transfer barrier under confinement is governed by electronic rather than geometric factors, providing a mechanistic design principle for tailoring proton conduction and chemical reactivity through nanoscale confinement.
